a linear epitopic structure in the C4 molecule becomes hidden upon activation with C1(-s) or methylamine, and that this hidden epitope is involved in the hydrophobicity at the C- terminal portion of C4d.
the surface hydrophobic sequence in C4, which is hidden by the C1s-induced conformational change, is involved in the linear epitope for the monoclonal antibody Al 121/5.

the surface structure of C4 becomes hidden upon activation, as a result of a conformation change induced by C1s and that the epitope recognized by mAb Al 12 1/6, which becomes hidden as a consequence, is located at the 1259-1264 sequence of C4d.

the identification of a surface epitope in C4 which is hidden upon activation by either C1(-) s or methylamine.
the identification of a surface structure, which becomes hidden into the inner region upon activation by C(-1)s.
the structural changes of C4 that are induced upon treatment with C(-)s and with methylamine.

the C4d molecule has a surface hydrophobic region which becomes hidden upon treatment with C4b and C1s and that the epitope recognized by mAb Al 1 21/6 is located at this region.
